subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should Docker multi-instance operation remain manual Compose/profile guidance for now?
rationale: The request defines new official operator UX and lifecycle semantics across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose names, updates, deletion, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Sponsor a core Docker lifecycle
options.body: Approve a minimal explicit design for named Docker instances with identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Leave this as a design backlog item while relying on the current multi-gateway docs, env variables, Docker setup script, and ClawDock helpers.

options.title: Route to external wrapper
options.body: Decline core ownership unless a missing core API is identified, and ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or ClawHub package around the current primitives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core Docker lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a minimal explicit design for named Docker instances with identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate from current multi-gateway docs and adjacent Docker/setup history.
